approach: Add a gate rule next to the open-questions rule in `plan_findings` that refuses a plan whose risks, or whose dependents' tests and reasons, hand caller and test discovery to the producer. One helper, `defers_to_producer(text)`, normalizes the text into words (lowercase, markup removed, `producer's` read as `producer`). It matches only a discovery deferral: the word `producer`, zero or more auxiliaries, an inflected discovery verb, and an impact word (callers, readers, tests, existing, crates, include_str, and so on) within eight words after the verb, with no procedural marker (cargo, pass, fmt, clippy) in that window. It also matches `left/leave (it) to the producer` when the same text names an impact word. So 'producer to check existing go tests' is refused, while 'the producer should check that cargo fmt passes' and 'the producer will verify with cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets' are accepted. `risks_findings` emits one Major Athena finding per offending risk at location `risks`; `dependents_deferral_findings` emits one at `dependents, dependent N`. Both are called from `plan_findings` after `open_questions_findings`, and a Major finding returns the plan to the planner with no critic call. The doc comment names the root cause and says plainly what the rule cannot see: an omission with no written deferral (job 20261026-193430-avnq's unlisted include_str! reader) is covered only by the new planner.md line, which is prose. The `open_questions_findings` doc comment is corrected to match. One line goes into planner.md, the `budget planner` line in docs/system-facts.md is recomputed, and CHANGELOG.md gets an entry. Tests are unit tests in admission.rs and a case table in refusal_corpus.rs.

decisions.choice: Fix at `plan_findings` with a risks rule and a dependents-deferral rule that share one helper `defers_to_producer`, and add one planner.md line.
decisions.reason: `open_questions_findings` (admission.rs:331) never reads risks, and its doc (admission.rs:325-326) says the caller listing 'stays prose'. Job 20261025-055626-er96 passed the gate with a risk deferring to the producer. The planner brief points callers to `dependents`, and `dependents_findings` (admission.rs:383) accepts any non-blank test or reason, so a risks-only rule would push the deferral into dependents. Scanning both places closes the written-deferral half of the class. The other half, an omission with no written deferral (job 20261026-193430-avnq), cannot be seen by a text rule; only the planner.md line addresses it, and that line is prose only. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say so.

rejected.why: Prose alone is what failed twice; the user default 'mechanism' wants enforcement in code.
The deferral would move into a dependent's reason.

decisions.choice: Answer critic finding 2: the matcher requires an impact word within eight words after the discovery verb and no procedural marker in that window. Procedural markers are cargo, pass, passes, passing, green, fmt, clippy, succeed, succeeds. Verbs are check, verify, search, find, grep, determine, their -s forms, and look(s) for. Zero or more auxiliaries (to, should, will, must, needs, has, also, then, can, may) may sit between `producer` and the verb.
decisions.reason: `check` and `verify` are used procedurally as often as `confirm`. Requiring an impact object (the option-two fix) refuses 'producer to check existing go tests' and 'producer should verify the callers' but not 'the producer should check that cargo fmt --check passes' (no impact word, and cargo/passes are markers) or 'the producer will verify with cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets' (cargo marker; `test` singular is not an impact word). The marker rule also accepts 'the producer should verify the existing tests pass', a procedural sentence that contains an impact word. Over-refusal is costly because MAX_MECHANICAL_PASSES is 2 (planning.rs:437) and the job stops after that. The corpus pins both directions.

rejected.option: Match the verb list without an impact object
rejected.why: Refuses ordinary procedural mitigations, as the critic showed.

rejected.option: Do not match when check/verify is followed by `that`
rejected.why: 'check that no other crate reads display.rs' is a real deferral.

rejected.option: Include the singular `test` as an impact word
rejected.why: It appears in `cargo test` and 'test output'; a miss costs a critic round, a false refusal costs a mechanical pass. Listed as a known miss.
A transparent word list, like `says_code_answers` (admission.rs:366), is simple and the corpus pins it.

decisions.choice: Answer critic nit 5: normalize `producer's` and `producer’s` to `producer`, accept the inflected verbs (checks, verifies, searches, finds, greps, determines, looks for), and allow zero auxiliaries. Known misses go in the doc comment: the passive ('callers to be checked by the producer'), an adverb between auxiliary and verb ('producer to carefully check'), and the singular `test` as the only impact word.
decisions.reason: The inflected and possessive forms cost a few lines. The impact-object requirement keeps zero-auxiliary matches from refusing 'the producer finds the figure in the failure message'. The passive and adverb forms need grammar parsing; the critic still reviews what passes.

rejected.why: Needs a parse; the rule is a declaration check, not proof.

steps: In crates/athena-core/src/admission.rs add `fn defers_to_producer(text: &str) -> bool`. Normalize: lowercase, remove `*` and backticks, split on whitespace, trim non-alphanumeric characters from each word's edges, and strip a trailing `'s` or `’s` (so `producer's` becomes `producer`). Form A: for each word equal to `producer`, skip zero or more auxiliaries (to, should, will, must, needs, has, also, then, can, may). If the next word is check, checks, verify, verifies, search, searches, find, finds, grep, greps, determine or determines, or is look/looks followed by `for`, take the next eight words as the window. The text defers when the window holds an impact word and no procedural marker. Impact words: caller, callers, reader, readers, tests, existing, crates, impact, dependent, dependents, usage, usages, references, or a word containing `include_str`. Procedural markers: cargo, pass, passes, passing, green, fmt, clippy, succeed, succeeds. Form B: the text holds the contiguous phrase 'left to the producer', 'leave to the producer' or 'leave it to the producer' and any word of the text is an impact word. Do not match read, confirm, review or inspect.

Add `fn risks_findings(risks: &[PlanRisk]) -> Vec<Finding>`: for each risk (numbered from 1), when `defers_to_producer` is true for its `risk` or its `mitigation`, push one `athena_finding(Severity::Major, "risks".into(), format!("Risk {n} defers its impact to the producer: {risk}"), detail)`. The detail says to search the tests and other crates, state the answer with file and line, and list the callers and tests in `dependents`. Add `fn dependents_deferral_findings(dependents: &[PlanDependent])`: for each dependent, when its present non-blank `test` or `reason` defers, push one Major finding at `dependents, dependent N` with summary 'Dependent N (<name>) defers its impact to the producer: <text>'. Put the root-cause doc comment on `risks_findings`: planning was not required to settle caller and test impact, and risks and dependents could say 'producer to check', so plans passed with impact open (job 20261025-055626-er96). State plainly that the rule refuses written deferrals only; an omission with no deferral (job 20261026-193430-avnq's unlisted include_str! reader of display.rs) is covered only by the planner.md line, which is prose. List the known misses (passive, adverb before the verb, singular `test` only). Include 'expected 5% of newly refused plans (the reading's estimate, not a measurement)' and that the higher refusal rate is intended because those plans cost critic rounds on impact the planner can find by searching. Import `PlanRisk` if it is not in scope (athena_data::records, admission.rs:24-27).

demonstrations.fails_without: Without the rule every Refuse case gets zero findings and the table test fails. Without the impact-object and procedural-marker conditions the Accept cases 'should check that fmt passes' and 'will verify with cargo test ... budgets' fail. Without the narrowed verb list the 'must read' and 'must confirm' cases fail.
demonstrations.seam: Entry point: `athena_core::admission::plan_findings`. Fixture: the corpus's existing `plan_side::plan_for(dependents)` plus `super::base_reading("")` with a content criterion, as `question_findings` does (refusal_corpus.rs:2668). The new `impact_findings(&ImpactCase)` helper sets `plan.risks` and the dependent's test and reason before the call. The harness shape exists; the table, case struct and helper are added by step 4. The matching logic stays in production code.

demonstrations.method: Content check: Grep planner.md for 'include_str!' and read the new line. Then run the budget tests.
demonstrations.observes: One line tells the planner to search the tests and other crates for the callers of every changed production path, for include_str! or fs reads of moved files and for output assertions, to list them in dependents, and never to leave them to the producer (Athena refuses a written deferral). The planner set stays within 1300 and docs/system-facts.md carries the recomputed `budget planner` figure.

demonstrations.method: Content check: Grep for '5% of newly refused plans' in admission.rs and CHANGELOG.md.
demonstrations.observes: The `risks_findings` doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry each say the rule refuses more plans, expected 5% of newly refused plans (the reading's estimate, not a measurement), and that the higher refusal rate is intended because those plans cost critic rounds on impact the planner can find by searching. The admission tests compile and pass with the comment in place.

demonstrations.method: Read the new CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased], then check the changed paths with git status and git diff.
demonstrations.observes: The entry names the root cause (planning was not required to settle caller and test impact, and risks and dependents could say 'producer to check', as in job 20261025-055626-er96), the two rules, and the limit: job 20261026-193430-avnq's unlisted reader is covered only by the planner.md prose line. It names briefs.rs `OPEN_QUESTION_RULE` as a follow-up. Changed paths are only admission.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, planner.md, planning.rs, CHANGELOG.md and docs/system-facts.md. display.rs is unchanged and display/status_view.rs does not exist.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole gate: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then `cargo test --workspace`, which includes budgets.rs, the refusal corpus and the athena-context wording tests.
demonstrations.observes: All pass. Fake planner outputs in run/tests.rs, lifecycle.rs, job_plan.rs and introspection.rs carry `"risks": []` and no deferral text, so none is refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the system-facts update, `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails. Without the rule none of the new tests pass.
demonstrations.seam: Whole-workspace run, no double. Existing tests that reach `plan_findings` indirectly with empty risks are the regression check.
